Below is the exact request you need to send to VirusTotal to cast a “malicious” vote for the IP 22.242.75.136.  
Just replace **`<YOUR_KEY_FOUR>`** with the real API key you have stored under the name *key_four*.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/22.242.75.136/votes" \
     -H "x-apikey: <YOUR_KEY_FOUR>" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
           "type": "vote",
           "attributes": {
             "verdict": "malicious"
           }
         }'
```

### What to expect

- **Success (HTTP 200)** – The response will contain the newly created vote object, e.g.:

  ```json
  {
    "data": {
      "id": "some-uuid",
      "type": "vote",
      "attributes": {
        "verdict": "malicious",
        "created_at": "2026-06-20T12:34:56Z",
        "updated_at": "2026-06-20T12:34:56Z"
      }
    }
  }
  ```

- **Error (HTTP 4xx/5xx)** – The body will include an `error` object explaining why the request failed (e.g., missing key, rate‑limit exceeded, etc.).

### Quick checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | API endpoint: `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/22.242.75.136/votes` |
| ✅ | HTTP method: `POST` |
| ✅ | Header `x-apikey`: your key (`key_four`) |
| ✅ | Header `Content-Type`: `application/json` |
| ✅ | Body JSON: `{"type":"vote","attributes":{"verdict":"malicious"}}` |

If you prefer a programmatic approach (Python, JavaScript, etc.), just wrap the same URL, headers, and JSON payload in your preferred HTTP client. Let me know if you’d like a snippet in a specific language!
